 Our warm stretch continues, with a few opportunities for rain 
 By Kira Miner Published : Oct. 27, 2026 at 12:07 PM CDT Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google Mostly cloudy today 
 Above average temperatures through the weekend 
 Rain prospects increase late this week 
 ROCKFORD, Ill. (Rockford News First) - After a much cooler start to the week, temperatures will begin to warm up over the next few days courtesy of southerly winds returning to the area. This will keep our unseasonably warm weather pattern locked in place with highs in the 60s and 70s through early next week.
 Mostly cloudy skies will prevail across northern Illinois today, with highs near 70° in some spots. A few breaks in the clouds are possible as we head into the afternoon, with mainly dry weather and light winds. 
 Partly sunny to mostly cloudy (Rockford News First) Click here for Interactive Radar
 Click here for Interactive Radar 
 What’s Coming Up...
 Clouds will begin to scatter out by Wednesday, with more sunshine in the forecast. This will also lead to a bump in our daytime highs, as temperatures top out in the lower to middle 70s. A cold front to our northwest, will eventually make it to northern Illinois late Wednesday night and into Thursday. This frontal boundary does have a bit more moisture to work with, so scattered showers will be possible throughout our Thursday. Rain should begin to wrap up by late in the day, with a slight cool down into Friday as winds shift to the north and east.
 A cold front will bring in a broken line of showers early Thursday (Rockford News First) Download the First Alert Weather app
 iPhone/iPad Android Looking Ahead...
 Don’t forget to “fall back” 1 hour before you head to bed Saturday night, as Daylight Saving Time officially comes to an end early Sunday morning. Another storm system developing early next week, could bring more widespread rain to the Midwest by Monday and Tuesday.
